c.tagline: East-coast gateway to Taroko Gorge — marble canyons, Pacific whales, and night-market feasts.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered with a flag-fall around NT$100 and wait outside the railway station; they are the easiest way to reach the airport, Qixingtan, and Taroko trailheads. Uber and the local yoxi app also operate.

emergency.note: 119 reaches fire and ambulance; 110 is police. English may be limited, so ask a local to help if possible.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable grid around Zhongzheng and Zhongshan Roads holding most of the city's restaurants, the Dongdamen Night Market, and buses to Taroko; Hualien's dining and nightlife heart.
The area beside Hualien Railway Station, packed with business hotels and guesthouses, scooter and bike rentals, and gorge-bound buses from the forecourt; the most transit-efficient base.
A resort-grade oceanfront district north of the center below pine-covered Meilun Hill, with the widest beaches, Pacific sunrises, and the Japanese-era Pine Garden.
A relaxed residential shore below the Meilun River mouth, with the Nanbin Park cycling path, pebbled Pacific beach, and family-run guesthouses.
A crescent pebble bay toward the airport prized for sunrise and stargazing; mostly small B&Bs, so many visitors base in Meilun or the center and drive over.

water.note: Tap water is treated but locals boil it; drink boiled or bottled.

transit.hours: Trains run roughly 5 AM to midnight; local and tourist-shuttle buses run mainly daytime (about 6 AM to 9 PM) with sparse frequency, so scooters, bikes, and taxis fill the gaps.
transit.note: Hualien City centers on its Taiwan Railway station, the east-coast rail hub with frequent Puyuma and Taroko expresses to Taipei (~2 hours). Local bus service is thin, so many visitors rent a scooter or take taxis and tours to reach Taroko Gorge, Qixingtan, and the East Rift Valley.
transit.pay: Trains are paid with EasyCard, iPASS, or tickets at Hualien Station; local and Taroko-bound buses take EasyCard/iPASS contactless or cash to the driver. High-speed THSR rail does not reach the east coast — connect via conventional Taiwan Railway or bus.

car.idp: Required (International Driving Permit needed with home license)

train: Taiwan Railway east-coast main line (Hualien Station) — Puyuma/Taroko expresses to Taipei and south to Taitung

transit.m: Local bus / Taroko shuttle toward the city

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Taiwan; a 10% service charge is often added at hotels and higher-end restaurants, so no extra is expected.
